Option<i32>,\n228\t    /// Duration of the test run in milliseconds.\n229\t    pub duration_ms: u64,\n230\t    /// Whether the test timed out.\n231\t    pub timed_out: bool,\n232\t    /// Length of captured stdout in bytes.\n233\t    pub stdout_len: usize,\n234\t    /// Length of captured stderr in bytes.\n235\t    pub stderr_len: usize,\n236\t    /// When the test completed.\n237\t    pub timestamp: chrono::DateTime<chrono::Utc>,\n238\t}\n239\t\n240\timpl TestMetrics {\n241\t    /// Returns true if the test succeeded (exit code 0 and no timeout).\n242\t    pub fn success(&self) -> bool {\n243\t        self.exit_code == Some(0) && !self.timed_out\n244\t    }\n245\t\n246\t    /// Get the duration as a Duration.\n247\t    pub fn duration(&self) -> Duration {\n248\t        Duration::from_millis(self.duration_ms)\n249\t    }\n250\t}\n251\t\n252\t// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n253\t// Compilation Error Detection\n254\t// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n255\t\n256\t/// Detect compilation errors from cargo test stderr.\n257\t///\n258\t/// Returns (compilation_failed, error_messages) where compilation_failed is true\n259\t/// if stderr contains compilation error patterns, and error_messages is a list\n260\t/// of parsed error messages.\n261\tpub fn detect_compilation_errors(stderr: &str) -> (bool, Vec<String>) {\n262\t    let mut compilation_failed = false;\n263\t    let mut error_messages = Vec::new();\n264\t\n265\t    // Cargo compilation error patterns\n266\t    // 1. \"error[E####]: \" - Rust compiler errors with error codes\n267\t    // 2. \"error: could not compile \" - Compilation failed message\n268\t    // 3. \"error: aborting due to \" - Abort message\n269\t    // 4. \"error: \" followed by a filename - General compilation errors\n270\t\n271\t    for line in stderr.lines() {\n272\t        let line = line.trim();\n273\t\n274\t        // Check for Rust compiler error codes (e.g., \"error[E0308]:\")\n275\t        if line.starts_with(\"error[E\") {\n276\t            compilation_failed = true;\n277\t            if let Some(msg) = parse_error_line(line) {\n278\t                error_messages.push(msg);\n279\t            }\n280\t            continue;\n281\t        }\n282\t\n283\t        // Check for \"could not compile\" message\n284\t        if line.contains(\"could not compile\") {\n285\t            compilation_failed = true;\n286\t            if let Some(crate_name) = extract_crate_name(line) {\n287\t                error_messages.push(format!(\"Failed to compile crate: {}\", crate_name));\n288\t            } else {\n289\t                error_messages.push(\"Compilation failed\".to_string());\n290\t            }\n291\t            continue;\n292\t        }\n293\t\n294\t        // Check for \"aborting due to\" message\n295\t        // Only count this if we've already seen actual compilation errors\n296\t        if line.contains(\"aborting due to\") && compilation_failed {\n297\t            if let Some(count) = extract_error_count(line) {\n298\t                error_messages.push(format!(\"Aborted due to {} error(s)\", count));\n299\t            }\n300\t            continue;\n301\t        }\n302\t\n303\t        // Check for general \"error:\" messages (but not warnings)\n304\t        if line.starts_with(\"error:\") && !line.starts_with(\"error[E\") {\n305\t            // Only capture if it looks like a compilation error, not a test error\n306\t            if line.contains(\"unused\") || line.contains(\"dead_code\") || line.contains(\"mutability\") {\n307\t                // These are compiler warnings/lints, not test failures\n308\t                compilation_failed = true;\n309\t                error_messages.push(line.to_string());\n310\t            }\n311\t        }\n312\t    }\n313\t\n314\t    (compilation_failed, error_messages)\n315\t}\n316\t\n317\t/// Parse an error line to extract the error message.\n318\t///\n319\t/// Input: \"error[E0308]: mismatched types\"\n320\t/// Output: Some(\"E0308: mismatched types\")\n321\tfn parse_error_line(line: &str) -> Option<String> {\n322\t    // Extract everything after \"error[\" until end of line\n323\t    if let Some(start) = line.find(\"error[\") {\n324\t        if let Some(end) = line.find(']') {\n325\t            let error_code = &line[start + 6..end]; // Skip \"error[\"\n326\t            let message = line[end + 1..].trim(); // Skip \"]\"\n327\t            // Check if message is empty or just a colon\n328\t            if !message.is_empty() && message != \":\" {\n329\t                return Some(format!(\"{}: {}\", error_code, message));\n330\t            }\n331\t        }\n332\t    }\n333\t    None\n334\t}\n335\t\n336\t/// Extract crate name from \"could not compile\" message.\n337\t///\n338\t/// Input: \"error: could not compile `my_crate`\"\n339\t/// Output: Some(\"my_crate\")\n340\tfn extract_crate_name(line: &str) -> Option<String> {\n341\t    if let Some(start) = line.find('`') {\n342\t        if let Some(end) = line.rfind('`') {\n343\t            if start < end {\n344\t                return Some(line[start + 1..end].to_string());\n345\t            }\n346\t        }\n347\t    }\n348\t    None\n349\t}\n350\t\n351\t/// Extract error count from \"aborting due to\" message.\n352\t///\n353\t/// Input: \"aborting due to 3 previous errors\"\n354\t/// Output: Some(3)\n355\tfn extract_error_count(line: &str) -> Option<usize> {\n356\t    // Find the number in the line\n357\t    let words: Vec<&str> = line.split_whitespace().collect();\n358\t    for word in words {\n359\t        if let Ok(n) = word.parse::<usize>() {\n360\t            return Some(n);\n361\t        }\n362\t    }\n363\t    None\n364\t}\n365\t\n366\t// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n367\t// Cargo Test Runner\n368\t// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n369\t\n370\t/// Runner for cargo test commands.\n371\t///\n372\t/// ## Example\n373\t///\n374\t/// ```no_run\n375\t/// CargoTest {\n386\t    /// Workspace directory where cargo will run.\n387\t    workspace: PathBuf,\n388\t    /// Test arguments.\n389\t    args: TestArgs,\n390\t    /// Timeout in seconds.\n391\t {\n398\t            workspace: workspace.to_path_buf(),\n399\t            args: TestArgs::default(),\n400\t            timeout_secs: DEFAULT_TEST_TIMEOUT_SECS,\n401\t        }\n402\t    }\n403\t\n404\t    /// Create a new cargo test runner with custom arguments.\n405\t    pub fn with_args(workspace: &Path, args: TestArgs) -> Self {\n406\t        CargoTest {\n407\t            workspace: workspace.to_path_buf(),\n408\t            args,\n409\t            timeout_secs: DEFAULT_TEST_TIMEOUT_SECS,\n410\t        }\n411\t    }\n412\t\n413\t    /// Set a custom timeout (default is 600 seconds).\n414\t    pub fn with_timeout(mut self, timeout_secs: u64) -> Self {\n415\t        self.timeout_secs = timeout_secs;\n416\t        self\n417\t    }\n418\t\n419\t    /// Run cargo test with the configured arguments.\n420\t    ///\n421\t    /// ## Errors\n422\t    ///\n423\t    /// Returns an error if:\n424\t    /// - The cargo binary cannot be found\n425\t    /// - The workspace directory is invalid\n426\t    /// - The process cannot be spawned\n427\t    pub fn run(&self) -> Result<TestOutcome> {\n428\t        let start = Instant::now();\n429\t        let args = self.args.build_args();\n430\t\n431\t        tracing::info!(\n432\t            workspace = %self.workspace.display(),\n433\t            args = ?args,\n434\t            \"running cargo test\"\n435\t        );\n436\t\n437\t        // Build the cargo command\n438\t        let mut cmd = Command::new(\"cargo\");\n439\t        cmd.args(&args);\n440\t        cmd.current_dir(&self.workspace);\n441\t        cmd.stdout(Stdio::piped());\n442\t        cmd.stderr(Stdio::piped());\n443\t\n444\t        // Spawn the process\n445\t        let mut child = cmd.spawn().context(\"failed to spawn cargo test\")?;\n446\t\n447\t        // Wait for completion with timeout\n448\t        let timeout = Duration::from_secs(self.timeout_secs);\n449\t        let _exit_status = loop {\n450\t            match child.try_wait() {\n451\t                Ok(Some(status)) => break status,\n452\t                Ok(None) => {\n453\t                    if start.elapsed() >= timeout {\n454\t                        child\n455\t                            .kill()\n456\t                            .context(\"failed to kill cargo test after timeout\")?;\n457\t                        return Ok(TestOutcome {\n458\t                            exit_code: None,\n459\t                            stdout: String::new(),\n460\t                            stderr: String::from(\"command timed out\"),\n461\t                            duration: start.elapsed(),\n462\t                            timed_out: true,\n463\t                            compilation_failed: false,\n464\t                            compilation_errors: Vec::new(),\n465\t                        });\n466\t                    }\n467\t                    std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(100));\n468\t                }\n469\t                Err(e) => {\n470\t                    return Err(anyhow::anyhow!(\"failed to wait for cargo test: {}\", e));\n471\t                }\n472\t            }\n473\t        };\n474\t\n475\t        // Capture output\n476\t        let output = child\n477\t            .wait_with_output()\n478\t            .context(\"failed to capture cargo test output\")?;\n479\t\n480\t        let stdout = truncate_output(&String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout));\n481\t        let stderr = truncate_output(&String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr));\n482\t\n483\t        // Detect compilation errors\n484\t        let (compilation_failed, compilation_errors) =\n485\t            detect_compilation_errors(&String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr));\n486\t\n487\t        tracing::info!(\n488\t            exit_code = ?output.status.code(),\n489\t            duration_secs = start.elapsed().as_secs(),\n490\t            success = output.status.success(),\n491\t            compilation_failed,\n492\t            compilation_error_count = compilation_errors.len(),\n493\t            \"cargo test completed\"\n494\t        );\n495\t\n496\t        Ok(TestOutcome {\n497\t            exit_code: output.status.code(),\n498\t            stdout,\n499\t            stderr,\n500\t            duration: start.elapsed(),\n501\t            timed_out: false,\n502\t            compilation_failed,\n503\t            compilation_errors,\n504\t        })\n505\t    }\n506\t\n507\t    /// Get the workspace directory.\n508\t    pub fn workspace(&self) -> &Path {\n509\t seconds.\n518\t    pub fn timeout_secs(&self) -> u64 {\n519\t        self.timeout_secs\n520\t    }\n521\t\n522\t    /// Run cargo test and write output to files.\n523\t    ///\n524\t    /// This Arguments\n528\t    ///\n529\t    /// * `test_name` - A unique identifier for the test (e.g., \"integration_test_1\")\n530\t    ///\n531\t    /// ## Errors\n532\t    ///\n533\t    /// Returns an error ```no_run\n541\t    /// use needle::cargo_test::CargoTest;\n542\t    /// use std::path::Path;\n543\t    ///\n544\t    /// let runner = CargoTest::new(Path::new(\"/workspace\"));\n545\t    /// let test to get the outcome\n549\t        let outcome = self.run()?;\n550\t\n551\t        // Create test output directory and write outputs\n552\t        if let Some(output) = TestOutput::new(test_name, &self.workspace) {\n553\t            // Write stdout\n554\t            if let Err(e) = output.write_stdout(&outcome.stdout) {\n555\t                tracing::warn!(\n556\t                    test_name = %test_name,\n557\t                    error = %e,\n558\t                    \"failed to write stdout to file\"\n559\t                );\n560\t            }\n561\t\n562\t            // Write = %e,\n567\t                    \"failed to write stderr to file\"\n568\t                );\n569\t            }\n570\t\n571\t            // Write combined output\n572\t            let combined = = %test_name,\n576\t                    error = %e,\n577\t                    \"failed to write combined output to file\"\n578\t                );\n579\t            }\n580\t\n581\t %output.stderr_path().display(),\n585\t                combined_path = %output.combined_path().display(),\n586\t                \"test output written to files\"\n587\t            );\n588\t        } else {\n589\t            tracing::warn!(\n590\t                test_name = %test_name,\n591\t                \"failed to create test output directory, output files not written\"\n592\t            );\n593\t        }\n594\t\n595\t        Ok(outcome)\n596\t    }\n597\t}\n598\t\n599\t// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n600\t// Utility Functions\n601\t// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n602\t\n603\t/// Truncate output to at most MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES.\n604\tfn truncate_output(s: &str) -> String {\n605\t    if s.len() <= MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES {\n606\t        s.to_string()\n607\t    } else {\n608\t        let truncated = &s[..MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES];\n609\t        format!(\"{}... combined.push('\\n');\n645\t        }\n646\t    }\n647\t\n648\t    combined\n649\t}\n650\t\n651\t// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n652\t// error_messages.push(line.to_string());\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    (compilation_failed, error_messages)\n}\n\n/// Parse an error line to extract the error message.\n///\n/// Input: error codes\n    // 2. \"error: could not compile \" - Compilation failed message\n    // 3. \"error: aborting due to \" - Abort message\n    // 4. \"error: \" followed by a filename - General Some(crate_name) = extract_crate_name(line) {\n                error_messages.push(format!(\"Failed to compile crate: {}\", crate_name));\n            } else {\n                error_messages.push(\"Compilation failed\".to_string());\n            }\n            continue;\n        }\n\n        // Check for \"aborting due to\" message\n        // Only count this if we've already seen actual compilation errors\n        if line.contains(\"aborting due to\") && compilation_failed {\n            if let Some(count) = extract_error_count(line) {\n                error_messages.push(format!(\"Aborted due to {} error(s)\", count));\n            }\n            continue;\n        }\n\n        // Check for general \"error:\" messages (but not warnings)\n        if line.starts_with(\"error:\") && !line.starts_with(\"error[E\") {\n            // Only capture if it looks like a compilation error, not a test error\n            if line.contains(\"unused\") || line.contains(\"dead_code\") || line.contains(\"mutability\") {\n                // These are compiler warnings/lints, not test failures\n                compilation_failed = true;\n                error_messages.push(line.to_string());\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    (compilation_failed, error_messages)\n}\n\n/// Parse an error line to extract the error message.\n///\n/// Input: \"error[E0308]: mismatched types\"\n/// Output: Some(\"E0308: mismatched types\")\nfn parse_error_line(line: &str) -> Option<String> {\n    // Extract everything after \"error[\" until end of line\n    if let Some(start) = line.find(\"error[\") {\n        if let Some(end) = line.find(']') {\n            let error_code = &line[start + 6..end]; // Skip \"error[\"\n            let message = line[end + 1..].trim(); // Skip \"]\"\n            // Check if message is empty or just a colon\n            if !message.is_empty() && message != \":\" {\n                return Some(format!(\"{}: {}\", error_code, message));\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    None\n}\n\n/// Extract crate name from \"could not compile\" message.\n///\n/// Input: \"error: could not compile `my_crate`\"\n/// Output: Some(\"my_crate\")\nfn extract_crate_name(line: &str) -> Option<String> {\n    if let Some(start) = line.find('`') {\n        if let Some(end) = line.rfind('`') {\n            if start < end {\n                return Some(line[start + 1..end].to_string());\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    None\n}\n\n/// Extract error count from \"aborting due to\" message.\n///\n/// Input: \"aborting due to 3 previous errors\"\n/// Output: Some(3)\nfn extract_error_count(line: &str) -> Option<usize> {\n    // Find the number in the line\n    let words: Vec<&str> = line.split_whitespace().collect();\n    for word in words {\n        if let Ok(n) = word.parse::<usize>() {\n            return Some(n);\n        }\n    }\n    None\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Cargo Test Runner\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Runner for cargo test commands.\n///\n/// ## Example\n///\n/// ```no_run\n/// use needle::cargo_test::{CargoTest, TestArgs};\n/// use std::path::Path;\n///\n/// let args = TestArgs::new()\n///     .with_target(\"--lib\")\n///     .with_filter(\"integration\");\n///\n/// let runner = CargoTest::with_args(Path::new(\"/workspace\"), args);\n/// let outcome = runner.run().unwrap();\n/// ```\npub struct CargoTest {\n    /// Workspace directory where cargo will run.\n    workspace: PathBuf,\n    /// Test arguments.\n    args: TestArgs,\n    /// Timeout in seconds.\n    timeout_secs: u64,\n}\n\nimpl CargoTest {\n    /// Create a new cargo test runner with default arguments.\n    pub fn new(workspace: &Path) -> Self {\n        CargoTest {\n            workspace: workspace.to_path_buf(),\n            args: TestArgs::default(),\n            timeout_secs: DEFAULT_TEST_TIMEOUT_SECS,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Create a new cargo test runner with custom arguments.\n    pub fn with_args(workspace: &Path, args: TestArgs) -> Self {\n        CargoTest {\n            workspace: workspace.to_path_buf(),\n            args,\n            timeout_secs: DEFAULT_TEST_TIMEOUT_SECS,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Set a custom timeout (default is 600 seconds).\n    pub fn with_timeout(mut self, timeout_secs: u64) -> Self {\n        self.timeout_secs = timeout_secs;\n        self\n    }\n\n    /// Run cargo test with the configured arguments.\n    ///\n    /// ## Errors\n    ///\n    /// Returns an error if:\n    /// - The cargo binary cannot be found\n    /// - The workspace directory is invalid\n    /// - The process cannot be spawned\n    pub fn run(&self) -> Result<TestOutcome> {\n        let start = Instant::now();\n        let args = self.args.build_args();\n\n        tracing::info!(\n            workspace = %self.workspace.display(),\n            args = ?args,\n            \"running cargo test\"\n        );\n\n        // Build the cargo command\n        let mut cmd = Command::new(\"cargo\");\n        cmd.args(&args);\n        cmd.current_dir(&self.workspace);\n        cmd.stdout(Stdio::piped());\n        cmd.stderr(Stdio::piped());\n\n        // Spawn the process\n        let mut child = cmd.spawn().context(\"failed to spawn cargo test\")?;\n\n        // Wait for completion with timeout\n        let timeout = Duration::from_secs(self.timeout_secs);\n        let _exit_status = loop {\n            match child.try_wait() {\n                Ok(Some(status)) => break status,\n                Ok(None) => {\n                    if start.elapsed() >= timeout {\n                        child\n                            .kill()\n                            .context(\"failed to kill cargo test after timeout\")?;\n                        return Ok(TestOutcome {\n                            exit_code: None,\n                            stdout: String::new(),\n                            stderr: String::from(\"command timed out\"),\n                            duration: start.elapsed(),\n                            timed_out: true,\n                            compilation_failed: false,\n                            compilation_errors: Vec::new(),\n                        });\n                    }\n                    std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(100));\n                }\n                Err(e) => {\n                    return Err(anyhow::anyhow!(\"failed to wait for cargo test: {}\", e));\n                }\n            }\n        };\n\n        // Capture output\n        let output = child\n            .wait_with_output()\n            .context(\"failed to capture cargo test output\")?;\n\n        let stdout = truncate_output(&String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout));\n        let stderr = truncate_output(&String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr));\n\n        // Detect compilation errors\n        let (compilation_failed, compilation_errors) =\n            detect_compilation_errors(&String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr));\n\n        tracing::info!(\n            exit_code = ?output.status.code(),\n            duration_secs = start.elapsed().as_secs(),\n            success = output.status.success(),\n            compilation_failed,\n            compilation_error_count = compilation_errors.len(),\n            \"cargo test completed\"\n        );\n\n        Ok(TestOutcome {\n            exit_code: output.status.code(),\n            stdout,\n            stderr,\n            duration: start.elapsed(),\n            timed_out: false,\n            compilation_failed,\n            compilation_errors,\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Get the workspace directory.\n    pub fn workspace(&self) -> &Path {\n        &self.workspace\n    }\n\n    /// Get the test arguments.\n    pub fn args(&self) -> &TestArgs {\n        &self.args\n    }\n\n    /// Get the timeout in seconds.\n    pub fn timeout_secs(&self) -> u64 {\n        self.timeout_secs\n    }\n\n    /// Run cargo test and write output to files.\n    ///\n    /// This method runs `cargo test` and writes the captured stdout, stderr,\n    /// and combined output to separate files in the `.test_outputs/<test_name>/` directory.\n    ///\n    /// ## Arguments\n    ///\n    /// * `test_name` - A unique identifier for the test (e.g., \"integration_test_1\")\n    ///\n    /// ## Errors\n    ///\n    /// Returns an error if:\n    /// - The test run fails\n    /// - Output directory creation fails\n    /// - File writing fails\n    ///\n    /// ## Example\n    ///\n    /// ```no_run\n    /// use needle::cargo_test::CargoTest;\n    /// use std::path::Path;\n    ///\n    /// let runner = CargoTest::new(Path::new(\"/workspace\"));\n    /// let outcome = runner.run_with_output_files(\"my_test\").unwrap();\n    /// ```\n    pub fn run_with_output_files(&self, test_name: &str) -> Result<TestOutcome> {\n        // First run the test to get the outcome\n        let outcome = self.run()?;\n\n        // Create test output directory and write outputs\n        if let Some(output) = TestOutput::new(test_name, &self.workspace) {\n            // Write stdout\n            if let Err(e) = output.write_stdout(&outcome.stdout) {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    test_name = %test_name,\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"failed to write stdout to file\"\n                );\n            }\n\n            // Write stderr\n            if let Err(e) = output.write_stderr(&outcome.stderr) {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    test_name = %test_name,\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"failed to write stderr to file\"\n                );\n            }\n\n            // Write combined output\n            let combined = create_combined_output(&outcome.stdout, &outcome.stderr);\n            if let Err(e) = output.write_combined(&combined) {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    test_name = %test_name,\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"failed to write combined output to file\"\n                );\n            }\n\n            tracing::info!(\n                test_name = %test_name,\n                stdout_path = %output.stdout_path().display(),\n                stderr_path = %output.stderr_path().display(),\n                combined_path = %output.combined_path().display(),\n                \"test output written to files\"\n            );\n        } else {\n            tracing::warn!(\n                test_name = %test_name,\n                \"failed to create test output directory, output files not written\"\n            );\n        }\n\n        Ok(outcome)\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Utility Functions\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Truncate output to at most MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES.\nfn truncate_output(s: &str) -> String {\n    if s.len() <= MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES {\n        s.to_string()\n    } else {\n        let truncated = &s[..MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES];\n        format!(\"{}... [truncated]\", truncated)\n    }\n}\n\n/// Create combined output from stdout and stderr.\n///\n/// This function combines stdout and stderr into a single string with section headers.\n///\n/// ## Example\n///\n/// ```\n/// use needle::cargo_test::create_combined_output;\n///\n/// let stdout = \"Test output line 1\\nTest output line 2\";\n/// let stderr = \"Error message\";\n/// let combined = create_combined_output(stdout, stderr);\n/// ```\npub fn create_combined_output(stdout: &str, stderr: &str) -> String {\n    let mut combined = String::new();\n\n    if !stdout.is_empty() {\n        combined.push_str(\"=== STDOUT ===\\n\");\n        combined.push_str(stdout);\n        if !stdout.ends_with('\\n') {\n            combined.push('\\n');\n        }\n    }\n\n    if !stderr.is_empty() {\n        if !combined.is_empty() {\n            combined.push('\\n');\n        }\n        combined.push_str(\"=== STDERR ===\\n\");\n        combined.push_str(stderr);\n        if !stderr.ends_with('\\n') {\n            combined.push('\\n');\n        }\n    }\n\n    combined\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Tests\n// Vec<String>) {\n    let mut compilation_failed = false;\n    let mut error_messages = Vec::new();\n\n    // Cargo compilation error patterns\n    // 1. \"error[E####]: \" - Rust compiler errors with error codes\n    // 2. \"error: could not compile \" - Compilation failed message\n    // 3. \"error: aborting due to \" - Abort message\n    // 4. \"error: \" followed by a filename - General Some(crate_name) = extract_crate_name(line) {\n                error_messages.push(format!(\"Failed to compile crate: {}\", crate_name));\n            } else {\n                error_messages.push(\"Compilation failed\".to_string());\n            }\n            continue;\n        }\n\n        // Check for \"aborting due to\" message\n        // Only count this if we've already seen actual compilation errors\n        if line.contains(\"aborting due to\") && compilation_failed {\n            if let Some(count) = extract_error_count(line) {\n                error_messages.push(format!(\"Aborted due to {} error(s)\", count));\n            }\n            continue;\n        }\n\n        // Check for general \"error:\" messages (but not warnings)\n        if line.starts_with(\"error:\") && !line.starts_with(\"error[E\") {\n            // Only capture if it looks like a compilation error, not a test error\n            if line.contains(\"unused\") || line.contains(\"dead_code\") || line.contains(\"mutability\") {\n                // These are compiler warnings/lints, not test failures\n                compilation_failed = true;\n                error_messages.push(line.to_string());\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    (compilation_failed, error_messages)\n}\n\n/// Parse an error line to extract the error message.\n///\n/// Input: \"error[E0308]: mismatched types\"\n/// Output: Some(\"E0308: mismatched types\")\nfn parse_error_line(line: &str) -> Option<String> {\n    // Extract everything after \"error[\" until end of line\n    if let Some(start) = line.find(\"error[\") {\n        if let Some(end) = line.find(']') {\n            let error_code = &line[start + 6..end]; // Skip \"error[\"\n            let message = line[end + 1..].trim(); // Skip \"]\"\n            // Check if message is empty or just a colon\n            if !message.is_empty() && message != \":\" {\n                return Some(format!(\"{}: {}\", error_code, message));\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    None\n}\n\n/// Extract crate name from \"could not compile\" message.\n///\n/// Input: \"error: could not compile `my_crate`\"\n/// Output: Some(\"my_crate\")\nfn extract_crate_name(line: &str) -> Option<String> {\n    if let Some(start) = line.find('`') {\n        if let Some(end) = line.rfind('`') {\n            if start < end {\n                return Some(line[start + 1..end].to_string());\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    None\n}\n\n/// Extract error count from \"aborting due to\" message.\n///\n/// Input: \"aborting due to 3 previous errors\"\n/// Output: Some(3)\nfn extract_error_count(line: &str) -> Option<usize> {\n    // Find the number in the line\n    let words: Vec<&str> = line.split_whitespace().collect();\n    for word in words {\n        if let Ok(n) = word.parse::<usize>() {\n            return Some(n);\n        }\n    }\n    None\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Cargo Test Runner\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Runner for cargo test commands.\n///\n/// ## Example\n///\n/// ```no_run\n/// use needle::cargo_test::{CargoTest, TestArgs};\n/// use std::path::Path;\n///\n/// let args = TestArgs::new()\n///     .with_target(\"--lib\")\n///     .with_filter(\"integration\");\n///\n/// let runner = CargoTest::with_args(Path::new(\"/workspace\"), args);\n/// let outcome = runner.run().unwrap();\n/// ```\npub struct CargoTest {\n    /// Workspace directory where cargo will run.\n    workspace: PathBuf,\n    /// Test arguments.\n    args: TestArgs,\n    /// Timeout in seconds.\n    timeout_secs: u64,\n}\n\nimpl CargoTest {\n    /// Create a new cargo test runner with default arguments.\n    pub fn new(workspace: &Path) -> Self {\n        CargoTest {\n            workspace: workspace.to_path_buf(),\n            args: TestArgs::default(),\n            timeout_secs: DEFAULT_TEST_TIMEOUT_SECS,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Create a new cargo test runner with custom arguments.\n    pub fn with_args(workspace: &Path, args: TestArgs) -> Self {\n        CargoTest {\n            workspace: workspace.to_path_buf(),\n            args,\n            timeout_secs: DEFAULT_TEST_TIMEOUT_SECS,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Set a custom timeout (default is 600 seconds).\n    pub fn with_timeout(mut self, timeout_secs: u64) -> Self {\n        self.timeout_secs = timeout_secs;\n        self\n    }\n\n    /// Run cargo test with the configured arguments.\n    ///\n    /// ## Errors\n    ///\n    /// Returns an error if:\n    /// - The cargo binary cannot be found\n    /// - The workspace directory is invalid\n    /// - The process cannot be spawned\n    pub fn run(&self) -> Result<TestOutcome> {\n        let start = Instant::now();\n        let args = self.args.build_args();\n\n        tracing::info!(\n            workspace = %self.workspace.display(),\n            args = ?args,\n            \"running cargo test\"\n        );\n\n        // Build the cargo command\n        let mut cmd = Command::new(\"cargo\");\n        cmd.args(&args);\n        cmd.current_dir(&self.workspace);\n        cmd.stdout(Stdio::piped());\n        cmd.stderr(Stdio::piped());\n\n        // Spawn the process with timeout handling\n        let timeout = Duration::from_secs(self.timeout_secs);\n        let output = loop {\n            // Try to spawn and wait for output with timeout\n            match cmd.output() {\n                Ok(output) => break output,\n                Err(e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::TimedOut => {\n                    return Ok(TestOutcome {\n                        exit_code: None,\n                        stdout: String::new(),\n                        stderr: String::from(\"command timed out\"),\n                        duration: start.elapsed(),\n                        timed_out: true,\n                        compilation_failed: false,\n                        compilation_errors: Vec::new(),\n                    });\n                }\n                Err(e) => {\n                    return Err(anyhow::anyhow!(\"failed to execute cargo test: {}\", e))\n                        .with_context(|| \"failed to spawn or execute cargo test\");\n                }\n            }\n        };\n\n        let stdout = truncate_output(&String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout));\n        let stderr = truncate_output(&String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr));\n\n        // Detect compilation errors\n        let (compilation_failed, compilation_errors) =\n            detect_compilation_errors(&String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr));\n\n        tracing::info!(\n            exit_code = ?output.status.code(),\n            duration_secs = start.elapsed().as_secs(),\n            success = output.status.success(),\n            compilation_failed,\n            compilation_error_count = compilation_errors.len(),\n            \"cargo test completed\"\n        );\n\n        Ok(TestOutcome {\n            exit_code: output.status.code(),\n            stdout,\n            stderr,\n            duration: start.elapsed(),\n            timed_out: false,\n            compilation_failed,\n            compilation_errors,\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Get the workspace directory.\n    pub fn workspace(&self) -> &Path {\n        &self.workspace\n    }\n\n    /// Get the test arguments.\n    pub fn args(&self) -> &TestArgs {\n        &self.args\n    }\n\n    /// Get the timeout in seconds.\n    pub fn timeout_secs(&self) -> u64 {\n        self.timeout_secs\n    }\n\n    /// Run cargo test and write output to files.\n    ///\n    /// This method runs `cargo test` and writes the captured stdout, stderr,\n    /// and combined output to separate files in the `.test_outputs/<test_name>/` directory.\n    ///\n    /// ## Arguments\n    ///\n    /// * `test_name` - A unique identifier for the test (e.g., \"integration_test_1\")\n    ///\n    /// ## Errors\n    ///\n    /// Returns an error if:\n    /// - The test run fails\n    /// - Output directory creation fails\n    /// - File writing fails\n    ///\n    /// ## Example\n    ///\n    /// ```no_run\n    /// use needle::cargo_test::CargoTest;\n    /// use std::path::Path;\n    ///\n    /// let runner = CargoTest::new(Path::new(\"/workspace\"));\n    /// let outcome = runner.run_with_output_files(\"my_test\").unwrap();\n    /// ```\n    pub fn run_with_output_files(&self, test_name: &str) -> Result<TestOutcome> {\n        // First run the test to get the outcome\n        let outcome = self.run()?;\n\n        // Create test output directory and write outputs\n        if let Some(output) = TestOutput::new(test_name, &self.workspace) {\n            // Write stdout\n            if let Err(e) = output.write_stdout(&outcome.stdout) {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    test_name = %test_name,\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"failed to write stdout to file\"\n                );\n            }\n\n            // Write stderr\n            if let Err(e) = output.write_stderr(&outcome.stderr) {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    test_name = %test_name,\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"failed to write stderr to file\"\n                );\n            }\n\n            // Write combined output\n            let combined = create_combined_output(&outcome.stdout, &outcome.stderr);\n            if let Err(e) = output.write_combined(&combined) {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    test_name = %test_name,\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"failed to write combined output to file\"\n                );\n            }\n\n            tracing::info!(\n                test_name = %test_name,\n                stdout_path = %output.stdout_path().display(),\n                stderr_path = %output.stderr_path().display(),\n                combined_path = %output.combined_path().display(),\n                \"test output written to files\"\n            );\n        } else {\n            tracing::warn!(\n                test_name = %test_name,\n                \"failed to create test output directory, output files not written\"\n            );\n        }\n\n        Ok(outcome)\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Utility Functions\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Truncate output to at most MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES.\nfn truncate_output(s: &str) -> String {\n    if s.len() <= MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES {\n        s.to_string()\n    } else {\n        let truncated = &s[..MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES];\n        format!(\"{}... [truncated]\", truncated)\n    }\n}\n\n/// Create combined output from stdout and stderr.\n///\n/// This function combines stdout and stderr into a single string with section headers.\n///\n/// ## Example\n///\n/// ```\n/// use needle::cargo_test::create_combined_output;\n///\n/// let stdout = \"Test output line 1\\nTest output line 2\";\n/// let stderr = \"Error message\";\n/// let combined = create_combined_output(stdout, stderr);\n/// ```\npub fn create_combined_output(stdout: &str, stderr: &str) -> String {\n    let mut combined = String::new();\n\n    if !stdout.is_empty() {\n        combined.push_str(\"=== STDOUT ===\\n\");\n        combined.push_str(stdout);\n        if !stdout.ends_with('\\n') {\n            combined.push('\\n');\n        }\n    }\n\n    if !stderr.is_empty() {\n        if !combined.is_empty() {\n            combined.push('\\n');\n        }\n        combined.push_str(\"=== STDERR ===\\n\");\n        combined.push_str(stderr);\n        if !stderr.ends_with('\\n') {\n            combined.push('\\n');\n        }\n    }\n\n    combined\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Tests\n// Vec<String>,\n    /// Additional test flags (e.g., \"--exact\", \"--ignored\").\n    pub test_flags: Vec<String>,\n}\n\nimpl TestArgs {\n    /// Create new empty test args.\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        Self::default()\n    }\n\n    /// Set the test target.\n    pub fn with_target(mut self, target: impl Into<String>) -> Self {\n        self.target = Some(target.into());\n        self\n    }\n\n    /// Set the test filter.\n    pub fn with_filter(mut self, filter: impl Into<String>) -> Self {\n        self.filter = Some(filter.into());\n        self\n    }\n\n    /// Add a test name to run.\n    pub fn add_test_name(mut self, name: impl Into<String>) -> Self {\n        self.test_names.push(name.into());\n        self\n    }\n\n    /// Add a cargo flag (e.g., \"--release\").\n    pub fn add_cargo_flag(mut self, flag: impl Into<String>) -> Self {\n        self.cargo_flags.push(flag.into());\n        self\n    }\n\n    /// Add a test flag (e.g., \"--exact\").\n    pub fn add_test_flag(mut self, flag: impl Into<String>) -> Self {\n        self.test_flags.push(flag.into());\n        self\n    }\n\n    /// Build the full command arguments for `cargo test`.\n    fn build_args(&self) -> Vec<String> {\n        let mut args = Vec::new();\n\n        // Add cargo flags first\n        for flag in &self.cargo_flags {\n            args.push(flag.clone());\n        }\n\n        // Add \"test\" subcommand\n        args.push(\"test\".to_string());\n\n        // Add target if specified\n        if let Some(ref target) = self.target {\n            args.push(target.clone());\n        }\n\n        // Add test flags\n        for flag in &self.test_flags {\n            args.push(flag.clone());\n        }\n\n        // Add test names if specified\n        for name in &self.test_names {\n            args.push(\"--\".to_string());\n            args.push(name.clone());\n        }\n\n        // Add filter if specified (and no test names)\n        if !self.test_names.is_empty() {\n            if let Some(ref filter) = self.filter {\n                args.push(format!(\"--filter={filter}\"));\n            }\n        }\n\n        args\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Test Outcome\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Result of running cargo test.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct TestOutcome {\n    /// Exit code from cargo test (None if killed by signal).\n    pub exit_code: Option<i32>,\n    /// Captured stdout (truncated to MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES).\n    pub stdout: String,\n    /// Captured stderr (truncated to MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES).\n    pub stderr: String,\n    /// Duration of the test run.\n    pub duration: Duration,\n    /// Whether the test timed out.\n    pub timed_out: bool,\n    /// Whether compilation failed (vs test failure).\n    pub compilation_failed: bool,\n    /// Parsed compilation error messages (if compilation_failed is true).\n    pub compilation_errors: Vec<String>,\n}\n\nimpl TestOutcome {\n    /// Returns true if cargo test exited with code 0.\n    pub fn success(&self) -> bool {\n        self.exit_code == Some(0) && !self.timed_out\n    }\n\n    /// Returns true if the failure was due to compilation errors.\n    pub fn is_compilation_failure(&self) -> bool {\n        self.compilation_failed\n    }\n\n    /// Returns true if the failure was due to test failures (not compilation).\n    pub fn is_test_failure(&self) -> bool {\n        !self.success() && !self.timed_out && !self.compilation_failed\n    }\n\n    /// Returns a human-readable summary of the outcome.\n    pub fn summary(&self) -> String {\n        if self.timed_out {\n            format!(\"Timed out after {:?}\", self.duration)\n        } else if self.compilation_failed {\n            format!(\n                \"Compilation failed with {} error(s) in {:?}\",\n                self.compilation_errors.len(),\n                self.duration\n            )\n        } else if self.success() {\n            format!(\"Passed in {:?}\", self.duration)\n        } else {\n            format!(\n                \"Failed with exit code {:?} in {:?}\",\n                self.exit_code, self.duration\n            )\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Convert this outcome to structured metrics.\n    pub fn to_metrics(&self, test_name: String) -> TestMetrics {\n        TestMetrics {\n            test_name,\n            exit_code: self.exit_code,\n            duration_ms: self.duration.as_millis() as u64,\n            timed_out: self.timed_out,\n            stdout_len: self.stdout.len(),\n            stderr_len: self.stderr.len(),\n            timestamp: chrono::Utc::now(),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Test Metrics\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Structured test metrics for storage and analysis.\n///\n/// This type captures the essential metrics from a test run in a\n/// serializable format that can be written to disk or sent to\n/// telemetry systems.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]\npub struct TestMetrics {\n    /// Name of the test that was run.\n    pub test_name: String,\n    /// Exit code from cargo test (None if killed by signal).\n    pub exit_code: Option<i32>,\n    /// Duration of the test run in milliseconds.\n    pub duration_ms: u64,\n    /// Whether the test timed out.\n    pub timed_out: bool,\n    /// Length of captured stdout in bytes.\n    pub stdout_len: usize,\n    /// Length of captured stderr in bytes.\n    pub stderr_len: usize,\n    /// When the test completed.\n    pub timestamp: chrono::DateTime<chrono::Utc>,\n}\n\nimpl TestMetrics {\n    /// Returns true if the test succeeded (exit code 0 and no timeout).\n    pub fn success(&self) -> bool {\n        self.exit_code == Some(0) && !self.timed_out\n    }\n\n    /// Get the duration as a Duration.\n    pub fn duration(&self) -> Duration {\n        Duration::from_millis(self.duration_ms)\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Compilation Error Detection\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Detect compilation errors from cargo test stderr.\n///\n/// Returns (compilation_failed, error_messages) where compilation_failed is true\n/// if stderr contains compilation error patterns, and error_messages is a list\n/// of parsed error messages.\npub fn detect_compilation_errors(stderr: &str) -> (bool, Vec<String>) {\n    let mut compilation_failed = false;\n    let mut error_messages = Vec::new();\n\n    // Cargo compilation error patterns\n    // 1. \"error[E####]: \" - Rust compiler errors with error codes\n    // 2. \"error: could not compile \" - Compilation failed message\n    // 3. \"error: aborting due to \" - Abort message\n    // 4. \"error: \" followed by a filename - General compilation errors\n\n    for line in stderr.lines() {\n        let line = line.trim();\n\n        // Check for Rust compiler error codes (e.g., \"error[E0308]:\")\n        if line.starts_with(\"error[E\") {\n            compilation_failed = true;\n            if let Some(msg) = parse_error_line(line) {\n                error_messages.push(msg);\n            }\n            continue;\n        }\n\n        // Check for \"could not compile\" message\n        if line.contains(\"could not compile\") {\n            compilation_failed = true;\n            if let Some(crate_name) = extract_crate_name(line) {\n                error_messages.push(format!(\"Failed to compile crate: {}\", crate_name));\n            } else {\n                error_messages.push(\"Compilation failed\".to_string());\n            }\n            continue;\n        }\n\n        // Check for \"aborting due to\" message\n        // Only count this if we've already seen actual compilation errors\n        if line.contains(\"aborting due to\") && compilation_failed {\n            if let Some(count) = extract_error_count(line) {\n                error_messages.push(format!(\"Aborted due to {} error(s)\", count));\n            }\n            continue;\n        }\n\n        // Check for general \"error:\" messages (but not warnings)\n        if line.starts_with(\"error:\") && !line.starts_with(\"error[E\") {\n            // Only capture if it looks like a compilation error, not a test error\n            if line.contains(\"unused\") || line.contains(\"dead_code\") || line.contains(\"mutability\") {\n                // These are compiler warnings/lints, not test failures\n                compilation_failed = true;\n                error_messages.push(line.to_string());\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    (compilation_failed, error_messages)\n}\n\n/// Parse an error line to extract the error message.\n///\n/// Input: \"error[E0308]: mismatched types\"\n/// Output: Some(\"E0308: mismatched types\")\nfn parse_error_line(line: &str) -> Option<String> {\n    // Extract everything after \"error[\" until end of line\n    if let Some(start) = line.find(\"error[\") {\n        if let Some(end) = line.find(']') {\n            let error_code = &line[start + 6..end]; // Skip \"error[\"\n            let message = line[end + 1..].trim(); // Skip \"]\"\n            // Check if message is empty or just a colon\n            if !message.is_empty() && message != \":\" {\n                return Some(format!(\"{}: {}\", error_code, message));\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    None\n}\n\n/// Extract crate name from \"could not compile\" message.\n///\n/// Input: \"error: could not compile `my_crate`\"\n/// Output: Some(\"my_crate\")\nfn extract_crate_name(line: &str) -> Option<String> {\n    if let Some(start) = line.find('`') {\n        if let Some(end) = line.rfind('`') {\n            if start < end {\n                return Some(line[start + 1..end].to_string());\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    None\n}\n\n/// Extract error count from \"aborting due to\" message.\n///\n/// Input: \"aborting due to 3 previous errors\"\n/// Output: Some(3)\nfn extract_error_count(line: &str) -> Option<usize> {\n    // Find the number in the line\n    let words: Vec<&str> = line.split_whitespace().collect();\n    for word in words {\n        if let Ok(n) = word.parse::<usize>() {\n            return Some(n);\n        }\n    }\n    None\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Cargo Test Runner\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Runner for cargo test commands.\n///\n/// ## Example\n///\n/// ```no_run\n/// use needle::cargo_test::{CargoTest, TestArgs};\n/// use std::path::Path;\n///\n/// let args = TestArgs::new()\n///     .with_target(\"--lib\")\n///     .with_filter(\"integration\");\n///\n/// let runner = CargoTest::with_args(Path::new(\"/workspace\"), args);\n/// let outcome = runner.run().unwrap();\n/// ```\npub struct CargoTest {\n    /// Workspace directory where cargo will run.\n    workspace: PathBuf,\n    /// Test arguments.\n    args: TestArgs,\n    /// Timeout in seconds.\n    timeout_secs: u64,\n}\n\nimpl CargoTest {\n    /// Create a new cargo test runner with default arguments.\n    pub fn new(workspace: &Path) -> Self {\n        CargoTest {\n            workspace: workspace.to_path_buf(),\n            args: TestArgs::default(),\n            timeout_secs: DEFAULT_TEST_TIMEOUT_SECS,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Create a new cargo test runner with custom arguments.\n    pub fn with_args(workspace: &Path, args: TestArgs) -> Self {\n        CargoTest {\n            workspace: workspace.to_path_buf(),\n            args,\n            timeout_secs: DEFAULT_TEST_TIMEOUT_SECS,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Set a custom timeout (default is 600 seconds).\n    pub fn with_timeout(mut self, timeout_secs: u64) -> Self {\n        self.timeout_secs = timeout_secs;\n        self\n    }\n\n    /// Run cargo test with the configured arguments.\n    ///\n    /// ## Errors\n    ///\n    /// Returns an error if:\n    /// - The cargo binary cannot be found\n    /// - The workspace directory is invalid\n    /// - The process cannot be spawned\n    pub fn run(&self) -> Result<TestOutcome> {\n        let start = Instant::now();\n        let args = self.args.build_args();\n\n        tracing::info!(\n            workspace = %self.workspace.display(),\n            args = ?args,\n            \"running cargo test\"\n        );\n\n        // Build the cargo command\n        let mut cmd = Command::new(\"cargo\");\n        cmd.args(&args);\n        cmd.current_dir(&self.workspace);\n        cmd.stdout(Stdio::piped());\n        cmd.stderr(Stdio::piped());\n\n        // Spawn the process with timeout handling\n        let timeout = Duration::from_secs(self.timeout_secs);\n\n        // Use a thread to handle output() with timeout\n        let cmd_clone = cmd; // Move command into the block\n        let output_result = std::thread::spawn(move || {\n            cmd_clone.output()\n        });\n\n        // Wait for thread completion with timeout\n        let output = loop {\n            if start.elapsed() >= timeout {\n                return Ok(TestOutcome {\n                    exit_code: None,\n                    stdout: String::new(),\n                    stderr: String::from(\"command timed out\"),\n                    duration: start.elapsed(),\n                    timed_out: true,\n                    compilation_failed: false,\n                    compilation_errors: Vec::new(),\n                });\n            }\n\n            // Check if thread is complete\n            if output_result.is_finished() {\n                match output_result.join() {\n                    Ok(Ok(output)) => break output,\n                    Ok(Err(e)) => {\n                        return Err(anyhow::anyhow!(\"failed to execute cargo test: {}\", e))\n                            .with_context(|| \"failed to spawn or execute cargo test\");\n                    }\n                    Err(_) => {\n                        return Err(anyhow::anyhow!(\"cargo test thread panicked\"));\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n\n            std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(100));\n        };\n\n        let stdout = truncate_output(&String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout));\n        let stderr = truncate_output(&String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr));\n\n        // Detect compilation errors\n        let (compilation_failed, compilation_errors) =\n            detect_compilation_errors(&String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr));\n\n        tracing::info!(\n            exit_code = ?output.status.code(),\n            duration_secs = start.elapsed().as_secs(),\n            success = output.status.success(),\n            compilation_failed,\n            compilation_error_count = compilation_errors.len(),\n            \"cargo test completed\"\n        );\n\n        Ok(TestOutcome {\n            exit_code: output.status.code(),\n            stdout,\n            stderr,\n            duration: start.elapsed(),\n            timed_out: false,\n            compilation_failed,\n            compilation_errors,\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Get the workspace directory.\n    pub fn workspace(&self) -> &Path {\n        &self.workspace\n    }\n\n    /// Get the test arguments.\n    pub fn args(&self) -> &TestArgs {\n        &self.args\n    }\n\n    /// Get the timeout in seconds.\n    pub fn timeout_secs(&self) -> u64 {\n        self.timeout_secs\n    }\n\n    /// Run cargo test and write output to files.\n    ///\n    /// This method runs `cargo test` and writes the captured stdout, stderr,\n    /// and combined output to separate files in the `.test_outputs/<test_name>/` directory.\n    ///\n    /// ## Arguments\n    ///\n    /// * `test_name` - A unique identifier for the test (e.g., \"integration_test_1\")\n    ///\n    /// ## Errors\n    ///\n    /// Returns an error if:\n    /// - The test run fails\n    /// - Output directory creation fails\n    /// - File writing fails\n    ///\n    /// ## Example\n    ///\n    /// ```no_run\n    /// use needle::cargo_test::CargoTest;\n    /// use std::path::Path;\n    ///\n    /// let runner = CargoTest::new(Path::new(\"/workspace\"));\n    /// let outcome = runner.run_with_output_files(\"my_test\").unwrap();\n    /// ```\n    pub fn run_with_output_files(&self, test_name: &str) -> Result<TestOutcome> {\n        // First run the test to get the outcome\n        let outcome = self.run()?;\n\n        // Create test output directory and write outputs\n        if let Some(output) = TestOutput::new(test_name, &self.workspace) {\n            // Write stdout\n            if let Err(e) = output.write_stdout(&outcome.stdout) {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    test_name = %test_name,\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"failed to write stdout to file\"\n                );\n            }\n\n            // Write stderr\n            if let Err(e) = output.write_stderr(&outcome.stderr) {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    test_name = %test_name,\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"failed to write stderr to file\"\n                );\n            }\n\n            // Write combined output\n            let combined = create_combined_output(&outcome.stdout, &outcome.stderr);\n            if let Err(e) = output.write_combined(&combined) {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    test_name = %test_name,\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"failed to write combined output to file\"\n                );\n            }\n\n            tracing::info!(\n                test_name = %test_name,\n                stdout_path = %output.stdout_path().display(),\n                stderr_path = %output.stderr_path().display(),\n                combined_path = %output.combined_path().display(),\n                \"test output written to files\"\n            );\n        } else {\n            tracing::warn!(\n                test_name = %test_name,\n                \"failed to create test output directory, output files not written\"\n            );\n        }\n\n        Ok(outcome)\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Utility Functions\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Truncate output to at most MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES.\nfn truncate_output(s: &str) -> String {\n    if s.len() <= MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES {\n        s.to_string()\n    } else {\n        let truncated = &s[..MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES];\n        format!(\"{}... [truncated]\", truncated)\n    }\n}\n\n/// Create combined output from stdout and stderr.\n///\n/// This function combines stdout and stderr into a single string with section headers.\n///\n/// ## Example\n///\n/// ```\n/// use needle::cargo_test::create_combined_output;\n///\n/// let stdout = \"Test output line 1\\nTest output line 2\";\n/// let stderr = \"Error message\";\n/// let combined = create_combined_output(stdout, stderr);\n/// ```\npub fn create_combined_output(stdout: &str, stderr: &str) -> String {\n    let mut combined = String::new();\n\n    if !stdout.is_empty() {\n        combined.push_str(\"=== STDOUT ===\\n\");\n        combined.push_str(stdout);\n        if !stdout.ends_with('\\n') {\n            combined.push('\\n');\n        }\n    }\n\n    if !stderr.is_empty() {\n        if !combined.is_empty() {\n            combined.push('\\n');\n        }\n        combined.push_str(\"=== STDERR ===\\n\");\n        combined.push_str(stderr);\n        if !stderr.ends_with('\\n') {\n            combined.push('\\n');\n        }\n    }\n\n    combined\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Tests\n// line.starts_with(\"error:\") && !line.starts_with(\"error[E\") {\n            // Only capture if it looks like a compilation error, not a test error\n            if line.contains(\"unused\") || line.contains(\"dead_code\") || line.contains(\"mutability\") {\n                // These are compiler warnings/lints, not test failures\n                compilation_failed = true;\n     duration: start.elapsed(),\n            timed_out: false,\n            compilation_failed,\n            compilation_errors,\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Get the workspace directory.\n    pub fn workspace(&self) -> &Path {\n        &self.workspace\n    }\n\n    /// Get the test arguments.\n    pub fn args(&self) -> &TestArgs {\n        &self.args\n    }\n\n    /// Get the timeout in seconds.\n    pub fn timeout_secs(&self) -> u64 {\n        self.timeout_secs\n    }\n\n    /// Run cargo test and write output to files.\n    ///\n    /// This method runs `cargo test` and writes the captured stdout, stderr,\n    /// and combined output to separate files in the `.test_outputs/<test_name>/` directory.\n    ///\n    /// ## Arguments\n    ///\n    /// * `test_name` - A unique identifier for the test (e.g., \"integration_test_1\")\n    ///\n    /// ## Errors\n    ///\n    /// Returns an error if:\n    /// - The test run fails\n    /// - Output directory creation fails\n    /// - File writing fails\n    ///\n    /// ## Example\n    ///\n    /// ```no_run\n    /// use needle::cargo_test::CargoTest;\n    /// use std::path::Path;\n    ///\n    /// let runner = CargoTest::new(Path::new(\"/workspace\"));\n    /// let outcome = runner.run_with_output_files(\"my_test\").unwrap();\n    /// ```\n    pub fn run_with_output_files(&self, test_name: &str) -> Result<TestOutcome> {\n        // First run the test to get the outcome\n        let outcome = self.run()?;\n\n        // Create test output directory and write outputs\n        if let Some(output) = TestOutput::new(test_name, &self.workspace) {\n            // Write stdout\n            if let Err(e) = output.write_stdout(&outcome.stdout) {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    test_name = %test_name,\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"failed to write stdout to file\"\n                );\n            }\n\n            // Write stderr\n            if let Err(e) = output.write_stderr(&outcome.stderr) {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    test_name = %test_name,\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"failed to write stderr to file\"\n                );\n            }\n\n            // Write combined output\n            let combined = create_combined_output(&outcome.stdout, &outcome.stderr);\n            if let Err(e) = output.write_combined(&combined) {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    test_name = %test_name,\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"failed to write combined output to file\"\n                );\n            }\n\n            tracing::info!(\n                test_name = %test_name,\n                stdout_path = %output.stdout_path().display(),\n                stderr_path = %output.stderr_path().display(),\n                combined_path = %output.combined_path().display(),\n                \"test output written to files\"\n            );\n        } else {\n            tracing::warn!(\n                test_name = %test_name,\n                \"failed to create test output directory, output files not written\"\n            );\n        }\n\n        Ok(outcome)\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Utility Functions\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Truncate output to at most MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES.\nfn truncate_output(s: &str) -> String {\n    if s.len() <= MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES {\n        s.to_string()\n    } else {\n        let truncated = &s[..MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES];\n        format!(\"{}... [truncated]\", truncated)\n    }\n}\n\n/// Create combined output from stdout and stderr.\n///\n/// This function combines stdout and stderr into a single string with section headers.\n///\n/// ## Example\n///\n/// ```\n/// use needle::cargo_test::create_combined_output;\n///\n/// let stdout = \"Test output line 1\\nTest output line 2\";\n/// let stderr = \"Error message\";\n/// let combined = create_combined_output(stdout, stderr);\n/// ```\npub fn create_combined_output(stdout: &str, stderr: &str) -> String {\n    let mut combined = String::new();\n\n    if !stdout.is_empty() {\n        combined.push_str(\"=== STDOUT ===\\n\");\n        combined.push_str(stdout);\n        if !stdout.ends_with('\\n') {\n            combined.push('\\n');\n        }\n    }\n\n    if !stderr.is_empty() {\n        if !combined.is_empty() {\n            combined.push('\\n');\n        }\n        combined.push_str(\"=== STDERR ===\\n\");\n        combined.push_str(stderr);\n        if !stderr.ends_with('\\n') {\n            combined.push('\\n');\n        }\n    }\n\n    combined\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Tests\n//
